claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-side deletion-protection setting.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-side deletion-protection setting.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` false) and still refuse to be deleted because of provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while not having provider-side deletion protection.

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and provider-side deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection enforced independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection enforced independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.

Pulumi's `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi (at the Pulumi engine/state level), whereas provider-level deletion-protection attributes are enforced by the provider or cloud API; the two layers are complementary, not substitutes.

The Pulumi docs page 'destroy-failures' under operations/troubleshooting has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's own `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error message names a URN and mentions `protect`.
A documentation page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ explaining how to remove the `protect` resource option.
A documentation page exists at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/run-program/ titled 'Running your program on refresh and destroy'.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` in the Pulumi GCP provider have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the provider.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi; the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are cloud-API-enforced deletion protections.
Azure Resource Manager returns the error code `ScopeLocked` when deleting a resource protected by a management lock.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.

For provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, setting the attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough; you must set it to false, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the Pulumi Azure Native provider for creating management locks.
A `CanNotDelete` Azure management lock, enforced by Azure Resource Manager, must be removed before the locked resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
